tools.name: trip_add
tools.description: Log one drive in the mileage log: the date, where from and to, the distance in miles or km, the purpose, and the category (business, medical, moving, charitable, personal). Returns its TR-YYYY-NNNN id. Free tier: 20 trips per calendar month, counted on the month of the trip date.

tools.name: trip_list
tools.description: List trips in the mileage log, oldest first: date, from, to, distance, category, and the amount each earns under the rate in force on its day (or the plain reason it is unpriced). Filter by date range and category. Reads only.

tools.name: trip_remove
tools.description: Remove one trip from the mileage log by its exact TR-YYYY-NNNN id, for entries made by mistake. The id is not reissued: a gap in the TR series is the record that a trip was removed.

tools.name: rate_set
tools.description: Set what one mile or km is worth for one category in one jurisdiction from a date forward: the jurisdiction label, the category, the rate per unit, the currency, and the date it takes effect. Rates form a series per jurisdiction and category, and each trip earns the rate in force on the day it was d

tools.name: rate_list
tools.description: List every mileage rate on file, grouped by jurisdiction and category with the effective-from dates in order: the series each trip is priced from. Reads only.

tools.name: mileage_summary
tools.description: The deductible mileage for a date range, per category: trips, distance kept per unit, the rate each trip earned (the one in force on its day), and the deductible amount, totalled per currency. Trips with no applicable rate are listed with the reason, not silently dropped. Defaults to the current cal

tools.name: mileage_export
tools.description: The mileage log as CSV, one row per trip, oldest first: date, from, to, distance, unit, category, the rate applied (the one in force on the trip's day), the currency and the amount, plus purpose, jurisdiction, effective_from and id. tools.name: license_status
tools.description: Report this endpoint's licence state for your token as JSON: the product, the tier free or pro, why it is not Pro, and the checkout URL. Call it to explain a free-tier refusal. No arguments, nothing changes.

tools.name: license_activate
tools.description: Turn Pro on for this connection with key, an MCPL1.<payload>.<signature> issued at checkout for this server or the bundle. Data under your token stays; a wrong or expired key changes nothing. license_status confirms it.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "mileage_summary" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.
